tickets.title: Lyric error rate: an ASR adapter, a license-verified G2P and phoneme error rate as a hard constraint that never touches approved lyrics
tickets.what_to_build: A candidate that sings the wrong words is caught, and Jon's words are never rewritten. A G2P or phonemizer is chosen only after its license row is verified; an espeak-ng-backed G2P (GPL) is allowed only inside the ASR/PER worker process, behind the process boundary, and never in the control service or the web bundle. An ASR worker adapter (Whisper or Qwen3-ASR, chosen after their license rows, its profile declared by a named contract-fix PR) transcribes the separated vocal into an ASR-transcript asset, kept apart from the approved lyrics; phoneme error rate is computed against the approved lyrics' phonemes and joins the hard constraints as the badge 'Lyric errors high', with its threshold read from the gate record. PER is shown on real candidates only after a validation record exists. In CI the fake-asr profile drives the whole path. Why blocked: T50 (lyric error rate reuses the internal separation and the analysis child jobs).
acceptance_criteria: The G2P's license row is verified before adoption, and a test fails if the control service's environment or the web bundle imports espeak-ng or the G2P. Evidence: the register diff and the dependency test in the Linux PR run.
With fake-asr returning a known transcript, PER equals a hand-computed value for a fixture lyric. Evidence: the PER test in CI.
The ASR transcript is its own asset, and the approved-lyrics record stays byte-identical after a PER job. Evidence: the separation test in CI.
Without a validation record, no PER badge renders on a non-synthetic candidate. Evidence: the gating test in CI.
tickets.notes: P4-5, C2. If no G2P passes its license check, the ticket closes with PER unavailable and labelled so.

tickets.title: Lyric error rate validated on the Mac with Jon's license acceptance for the ASR model (needs Jon)
tickets.what_to_build: The lyric-error badge reaches real candidates only after it is shown to work on singing. Jon accepts the ASR model's license in O7; the model downloads and passes conformance on mlx/m5pro. PER is validated on sung vocals whose words are human-verified: Jon's own sung captures of known lyrics, and transcripts of ACE smoke vocals that Jon checks and records as an owner act, never ACE output assumed to sing its lyrics; tolerances are fixed before the run. If it passes, the badge joins the hard constraints on real candidates; if not, PER stays hidden and the record says why. Why blocked: T51 (PER runs on the real separated vocal, and through it ACE's smoke candidates on the Mac); T72 (the PER pipeline it validates).
acceptance_criteria: The ASR license acceptance predates its download, and the download verifies. Evidence: the install evidence record ids.
The PER validation record holds the fixture set, the tolerances fixed before the run, and the result. Evidence: the validation evidence record id under docs/evidence/.
The product shows or hides the PER badge exactly as the record decides. Evidence: the registry read and a screenshot attached to the PR.
tickets.notes: Needs Jon: the ASR model's license acceptance (owner act). P4-5. Whisper and Qwen3-ASR accuracy on sung vocals is UNVERIFIED until this record exists.
tickets.owner_needs: Accepts the ASR model's license in O7; sings a few known lyrics; checks and records the words actually sung in the ACE vocals used.

tickets.title: Smoke-12 eval auditions on real engines: Jon listens to the preregistered smoke set (needs Jon)
tickets.what_to_build: Every route and engine profile faces Jon's kinds of song before any claim is made. With the preregistration hash committed first, the harness runs the smoke-12 briefs on real engines: ACE in every lane, R1 on bursts (each run quoted and approved by Jon) in individual-lane briefs, ACE-only pairs in llc briefs. Jon listens in eval auditions with reference anchors and hidden repeat pairs until the quota is met. Results are recorded with brief-clustered uncertainty and repeat-pair consistency; a short quota concludes inconclusive. Promotions and demotions happen only through the records, and the default pair of each lane is confirmed or demoted. Briefs that need v1-studio operations are recorded as not yet runnable until those operations exist; the three-reference role task is not runnable in v1 (B11 is v2); R1 briefs are not yet runnable if Jon declined the R1 burst. His verdicts on whole-form against per-section rendering decide that default. Why blocked: T55 (his hum fixtures and the chosen transcriber); T62 (R1 runs for real on an approved burst, or is recorded as declined); T69 (the anchors); T71 (eval-mode auditions, quotas, analysis and route-standing); T73 (the preregistration fixes lyric error rate among the operational gates); T57 (the MIDI chord seed brief needs chord symbols).
acceptance_criteria: The preregistration commit precedes the first smoke run's evidence. Evidence: the commit ids and CI's order check.
Smoke-12 verdicts are recorded with brief-clustered uncertainty and repeat-pair consistency, or the set concludes inconclusive. Evidence: the result evidence record ids under docs/evidence/.
Every paid brief run has a quote, Jon's approval and a reservation, and the month stays at or under the cap. Evidence: the ledger export attached to the PR.

Any route-standing or status change cites the smoke records and changes the plan as the record says, and no route's 'unbenchmarked routes' label drops (smoke is not a benchmark). Evidence: the route-standing record ids, a plan response and the registry diff in the PR.
tickets.notes: Needs Jon: listening time to meet the quota, verdicts, and approvals for the paid briefs (owner acts). P4-2, P4-3. Listening results are reported separately from engine results.
tickets.owner_needs: Listens through the smoke-12 eval auditions to quota; gives every verdict; approves each paid brief run.

tickets.title: BS.1770-4 against BS.1770-5 integrated loudness on stereo programme, recorded as evidence
tickets.what_to_build: The '-4' label on every loudness figure is kept or dropped on evidence. An independent stdlib implementation of the BS.1770-5 integrated-loudness changes for stereo programme runs beside pyloudnorm's BS.1770-4 on generated programme material (NeutralVoice mixes and test signals), and the differences are recorded as an evidence record. If they differ beyond a stated tolerance, measure gains a BS.1770-5 option and every report names which standard it used; otherwise the -4 label stays with a pointer to the record. Why blocked: T20 (the measurement path and its -4 label).
acceptance_criteria: The comparison record lists per-item differences in LU as decimal strings with the stated tolerance and the material's hashes. Evidence: the evidence record id under docs/evidence/.
The -5 implementation reproduces the standard's worked examples (hand-checked literals in the fixture). Evidence: the toleranced tests in the Linux PR run.
Every loudness report still names its standard and meter version after the change. Evidence: the report test in CI.

tickets.title: StudioEngine: AudioWorklet playback on SharedArrayBuffer rings fed by a decoding worker, with the latency readout and the Chromium requirement
tickets.what_to_build: The Studio plays many tracks without dropouts, whatever generation, disk or network work is running. StudioEngine in apps/web plays through an AudioWorklet with a SharedArrayBuffer ring per track, fed by a decode Web Worker that reads artifact byte ranges; nothing blocking runs on the render thread. It reports the output latency the browser gives and instruments Chrome's playbackStats. In a browser that is not Chromium-based, S10 says plainly that the Studio requires one. Exports never use it; they use the separate deterministic offline render. Its interface is the timeline contract, so a CPAL native engine can replace this one module if a playback gate fails. Why blocked: T13 (test audio is generated at test time); T24 (artifact audio is range-served by the API).
acceptance_criteria: With crossOriginIsolated true, 8 generated tracks play for 60 s in headless Chromium with zero ring underruns while the main thread is loaded with synthetic work. Evidence: the Playwright playback test in the Linux PR run.
Output latency and playbackStats readouts appear as numbers in S10. Evidence: the Playwright test with macOS nightly screenshots.
In a non-Chromium user agent S10 shows the requirement notice and starts no playback. Evidence: the browser-gate test in CI.
A lint fails if any module other than the export path imports the offline renderer, or if StudioEngine imports export code. Evidence: the boundary lint in CI.
tickets.notes: ADR-0013 (two clocks), ADR-0024. The real 8 tracks × 30 minutes gate on the Mac is its own ticket.

tickets.title: Studio timeline: tracks, clips, markers and the shared tempo map, transport, mixer, clip gain and fades, saved as revisions
tickets.what_to_build: Jon opens a keeper in the Studio and arranges and balances it. A timeline/1 revision is created from a keeper: tracks of clips that refer to artifacts at their native rate, MIDI clips in ticks, the tempo map shared with the MelodySpec, and SongForm sections as named markers. Every change is an immutable timeline revision on a named base (409 when stale), so every arrangement step can be undone. Transport offers play, pause, stop, return to start and a loop span with keyboard shortcuts. Each track has solo, mute, a fader, pan and a level meter with a numeric readout; each clip has gain and fades. Waveforms are drawn (wavesurfer 8 core for single waveforms; waveform-playlist evaluated against AURA's own timeline and the choice recorded), and the timeline zooms in bars and beats or in time. MIDI clips open in the same piano roll as the melody. Below 1024 px an editable list replaces the canvas. S10's container declares its slots and their fillers: inspector/replace-section (section replace), inspector/extend and inspector/dsp-clip-edits (extend and DSP edits), inspector/replace-line-word and lyrics-strip (lyric alignment), tracks/replacement (replacement tracks), drawer/stems (isolate original), meters/loudness (finishing), transport/gate-line (the playback gate) and track/instrument (the MIDI synth evaluation); it also shows the StudioEngine's browser notice. Markers carry each section's name and colour. Why blocked: T27 (MIDI clips are edited in the same piano roll); T32 (the timeline opens a keeper); T76 (playback).
acceptance_criteria: Opening a keeper creates timeline revision 1 whose markers equal the SongForm's section names and positions (ticks to frames by the TimeModel). Evidence: the StudioHarness tests in the Linux PR run.
A stale timeline base gets 409, and undo steps back through revisions without changing any artifact. Evidence: the revision tests in CI.
Transport, mixer and clip-gain controls work by keyboard, and every meter exposes a number. Evidence: the Playwright keyboard test in CI.
A MIDI clip edited in the timeline uses the piano-roll component and produces a new revision of that clip. Evidence: the Playwright test in CI.

waveform-playlist is scored against AURA's own timeline on criteria fixed in the PR before scoring (bundle size, 8-track redraw time, keyboard operability, license), with the decision; a test fails if the decision record is missing or a criterion is unscored. Evidence: the committed evaluation record and the test log in CI.
S10 passes the accessibility audit and the keyboard-only pass (canvas plus list alternative). Evidence: the Playwright accessibility report in CI.
tickets.notes: TB9. ADR-0013, ADR-0033. Never wavesurfer-multitrack. ADR-0014 (no desktop shell: the Studio is a browser app).

tickets.title: The Mac playback gate: 8 tracks for 30 minutes with no underruns and a responsive UI during a generation, plus the 16-track stretch gate
tickets.what_to_build: 'The Studio works here' becomes a measured claim on the Mac. On the build Mac, the self-hosted runner plays an 8-track timeline for 30 minutes in Chrome while an ACE generation runs, reading playbackStats for underruns and measuring UI response at the 95th percentile; it then measures the 16-track stretch gate the same way. The results are an evidence record against studio.playback.darwin, which computes smoke-passed only if the 8-track gate passes; Windows and Linux stay unverified. On the same runner, StudioHarness and the recovery test (crash, restart, reindex, backup and restore) pass against the real STUDIO volume, recorded as darwin per-OS evidence. UI p95 is measured as the playback capability's definition says. Why blocked: T47 (a real ACE generation runs during the gate); T77 (the Studio being gated).
acceptance_criteria: The gate record shows 0 underruns for 8 tracks × 30 minutes and UI p95 under 100 ms while an ACE generation ran, labelled MEASURED-LOCAL with Chrome's version. Evidence: the evidence record id under docs/evidence/.
The 16-track stretch result is recorded beside it, pass or fail. Evidence: the same record.
studio.playback.darwin computes smoke-passed and the Windows and Linux entries stay unverified. Evidence: the registry read in the PR.
S10's gate line shows the measured figures with their label and date. Evidence: a screenshot attached to the PR.
StudioHarness and the recovery test pass against the real STUDIO volume on the self-hosted runner. Evidence: the darwin per-OS evidence record ids.
tickets.notes: P5-1. X-49. If the gate fails, only StudioEngine is replaced (CPAL), per ADR-0013's reverse-if.

tickets.title: Section replace: an edit operation proposes two ACE repaint candidates, an audition decides, and the preservation check guards the keeper
tickets.what_to_build: Jon changes one part of his song without touching the rest, and 'local edit' is a check that can fail. Selecting a section in S10 proposes an edit operation (edit-operation/1): a mask set from the section markers and adjustable by hand, crossfades and locked context. It runs ACE repaint with the chunk mask (a repaint module added to the ACE adapter; fake-repaint in CI) and returns two candidates for a blind audition. The operation stays a proposal until Jon accepts one candidate. AURA composites every candidate: the original audio outside the mask and its crossfades, ACE's output inside. Every composite gets a preservation report: the working audio outside the mask and crossfades must be identical, sample for sample, in a declared rate, channel and sample-type domain (PCM samples, not headers); a failing candidate cannot be accepted, and the first differing sample position is reported. Accepting makes a new keeper revision; undo restores the previous revision by hash with no job. A whole-song re-render is never labelled a local edit. Each keeper has an edit history listing every operation, its candidates and the accepted one. An edit operation on an imported Suno mix is refused. Why blocked: T46 (the repaint module joins the ACE adapter core); T77 (the edit is scoped from the timeline's section markers).
acceptance_criteria: A planted one-sample change outside the mask fails the preservation check in CI, and the report names its position. Evidence: the planted-change test in the Linux PR run.
On fake-repaint, accepting a passing candidate creates keeper revision n+1, and undo restores revision n by hash with no job created. Evidence: the accept and undo tests in CI.
A request covering the whole song is labelled a re-render, not a local edit. Evidence: the labelling test in CI.
An edit operation on a Suno-source import is refused with its reason. Evidence: the refusal test in CI.
The edit flow passes the accessibility audit and the keyboard-only pass. Evidence: the Playwright accessibility report in CI.
tickets.notes: TB9, P5-2, P5-3. ADR-0017. Split in the design review: the real repaint on the Mac is its own evidence ticket, so this slice runs on fake-repaint alone. Accepting a real candidate needs Jon's verdict, which belongs to his own use.

tickets.title: Section replace on the Mac: the composite preservation check and ACE's raw chunk-mask deviation on the pinned commit
tickets.what_to_build: 'Local edit' is shown to hold on the real engine. On the self-hosted runner, in a temporary test store whose keeper is a real ACE render with a test-mode verdict (allowed only in a temporary store; the record is labelled 'hardware, non-listening'), a section replace runs real ACE repaint with the chunk mask. Each composite's preservation report must pass. Separately, ACE's raw deviation outside the mask, before compositing, is recorded as MEASURED-LOCAL chunk-mask evidence against a pass rule committed before the run. Why blocked: T47 (ACE is smoke-passed on mlx/m5pro); T79 (the edit operation, compositing and preservation check).
acceptance_criteria: Both real repaint composites carry passing preservation reports. Evidence: the evidence record id under docs/evidence/ with the reports' hashes.
ACE's raw deviation outside the mask is recorded with the pass rule committed in an earlier commit, pass or fail. Evidence: the chunk-mask record id and both commit ids.
tickets.notes: Split from the section-replace ticket in the design review so the fake-only Studio chain does not wait on owner gates. Hardware evidence, never listening evidence. ADR-0017.

tickets.title: Replacement tracks and Copy to Main Track: candidates in context on their own tracks, and a rebuild of the mix from retained sources
tickets.what_to_build: Alternatives never overwrite the original until Jon chooses, and a replaced part never ghosts underneath. Each edit candidate, and any replacement part, arrives on its own replacement track so Jon can compare it in context. 'Copy to main track' rebuilds the mix from retained sources through the deterministic offline render (analysis-offline-render) and never lays a new part over a mix that still holds the old one. Exports always use the offline render, never what the browser played. Why blocked: T79 (edit candidates are what the replacement tracks hold).
acceptance_criteria: Copy to main track produces a new mix whose offline render equals the render of the rebuilt clip list (bit-exact within one environment), and the old part's audio is absent from the result. Evidence: the rebuild test in the Linux PR run.
A replacement track can be compared in context and discarded without changing any keeper. Evidence: the Playwright test in CI.
Rendering the same timeline revision twice offline gives identical bytes, independent of playback. Evidence: the determinism test in CI.
tickets.notes: ADR-0006 (rebuild), ADR-0013. GLOSSARY: these are tracks, never 'take lanes'.

tickets.title: Extend, deterministic DSP edits and restyle: repaint at the start or end, crop, remove, reverse and fades, a restyle labelled a new performance, and speed held behind a stretch evaluation
tickets.what_to_build: Jon can add an intro or an outro, make exact simple cuts, and try a restyle without losing track of what is what. Extend runs repaint at the start or end, one pass at a time, through the edit-operation path with preservation of the existing audio. Crop, remove a section, reverse, and fade in and out are deterministic DSP edits with no model: instant, exact and recorded as DSP-edit records. A restyle (an ACE cover of a keeper) is labelled a new performance and its melody adherence is measured. Speed changes are offered only after Signalsmith Stretch passes its quality evaluation: objective criteria fixed before the run (pitch error, transient smearing and loudness change on generated test signals) here, then Jon's blind verdict on stretched against unstretched clips in its own ticket; until both pass, the control does not exist. Why blocked: T50 (a restyle's melody adherence is measured); T79 (extend uses the same edit-operation and preservation path).
acceptance_criteria: An extend at the end preserves every original sample (the preservation report passes) and adds the new audio after it. Evidence: the extend test on fake-repaint in the Linux PR run.
Each DSP edit's output equals a hand-computed result for a generated test signal (bit-exact). Evidence: the DSP-edit tests in CI.
A restyle candidate's provenance reads new performance and carries adherence. Evidence: the restyle test in CI.

The objective time-stretch evaluation is recorded pass or fail against thresholds committed before the run, and the speed control is absent from the DOM unless both it and Jon's blind listening record pass. Evidence: the evaluation record, both commit ids and the DOM test in CI.
tickets.notes: ADR-0017, D6, D7, C10. Signalsmith Stretch (MIT) is adopted only after its license row; SoundTouch would be a separate-process fallback; Rubber Band is never bundled.

tickets.title: Time-stretch listening: Jon's blind verdict on stretched against unstretched clips (needs Jon)
tickets.what_to_build: A stretching artefact never ships as a feature on an agent's say-so. A preregistered set of stretched and unstretched clips (generated material and one of Jon's keepers) is auditioned blind and level-matched; Jon's verdicts decide pass or fail against the rule fixed in the preregistration. Only a pass, together with the objective evaluation, shows the speed control. Why blocked: T82 (the objective evaluation and the speed control it unlocks).
acceptance_criteria: The preregistration precedes the audition, and the record holds Jon's verdicts and the outcome of the fixed rule. Evidence: the commit ids and the evidence record id.
tickets.notes: Needs Jon: listening. Added in the design review. Optional; does not block final QA, which lists it while open. ADR-0010, ADR-0017.
tickets.owner_needs: Listens blind to the stretched and unstretched clips and gives verdicts.

tickets.title: Lyric word alignment and line or word replace: an alignment evaluation on singing, a correction UI kept apart from approved lyrics, and scoped replace only after both checks pass (needs Jon)
tickets.what_to_build: A one-word change does not re-sing the verse, and word edits hit the right syllables. A lyric word-alignment component is chosen after its license row and declared by a named contract-fix PR; an LLC alignment profile declares lyric_languages ['en'] only, because WhisperX's French, German, Spanish and Italian aligners are non-commercial; Jon accepts its model license; it is evaluated on singing (fixture vocals with known word times) and the result recorded pass or fail. The alignment is its own asset, kept apart from the approved lyrics, and S10's lyrics strip lets Jon correct word boundaries by hand. Replace line and replace word (scoped repaint through the edit-operation path) are offered only when both the alignment evaluation and a scoped-repaint preservation check have passed; otherwise the controls do not exist and the strip says why. Why blocked: T72 (alignment builds on the ASR adapter and transcript assets); T79 (line and word replace are scoped edit operations).
acceptance_criteria: The alignment evaluation record holds the fixture set, the tolerance fixed in advance and the result. Evidence: the evaluation record id under docs/evidence/.
Hand-corrected word timings are saved as a new alignment asset, and the approved-lyrics record stays byte-identical. Evidence: the harness test in CI.
Replace line and replace word are absent from the DOM until both checks have passing records, and present after. Evidence: the gating test in CI.
The lyrics strip is keyboard-operable, with word times readable as text. Evidence: the Playwright accessibility report in CI.
tickets.notes: Needs Jon: the alignment model's license acceptance (owner act). D3, D9. WhisperX was evaluated on speech only; alignment on singing is UNVERIFIED until this record exists. A failing evaluation is an allowed outcome.
tickets.owner_needs: Accepts the alignment model's license in O7.

tickets.title: Isolate original: stems with their residual, sum-to-mixture and bleed checks, honest labels, lane-aware separators and stems onto tracks
tickets.what_to_build: Jon gets honest stems: what a separator produced, plus everything it left over. Isolate original runs an isolate profile (isolate-demucs or isolate-demucs-mlx, distinct from the internal separate profiles) on a keeper and stores the mixture, the stems and the residual as separated_source artifacts with derived_from edges, so Demucs's lanes and release blockers travel with every stem; stems plus residual rebuild the mix by construction, and the same sum is re-checked on the stored and exported files after any conversion as an integrity check that can fail. Bleed and residual energy are measured against thresholds committed in a gate record before the Mac run, and Jon can listen to each stem, the residual and the rebuilt mix. Stems read 'separated · unreviewed' until Jon's listening verdict on a real isolation records otherwise. The residual is always kept and audible. Stems are labelled isolated only when a separator produced them; any regenerated part is labelled a new performance, and ACE's extract task is treated as a re-perform, never as isolation. In an llc project isolation is refused, with the reason, until an LLC separator is allow-listed. RoFormer checkpoints load only from the allow-list this ticket owns, keyed on verified licenses and training-data reviews. Jon can insert one stem or all stems onto tracks, download a stem, and transcribe any stem to MIDI with per-note confidence. A Suno import is never separated by a machine-learning model; the refusal points to Suno's own stems. Separation output is budgeted in the disk preflight at about 87.9 MiB per four-minute stereo float32 stem. Why blocked: T36 (stem-to-MIDI uses an admitted transcriber); T49 (the separator worker its isolate profiles extend); T77 (stems are inserted onto timeline tracks).
acceptance_criteria: On fake-isolate, stems plus residual sum to the mixture, a planted dropped band shows up in the residual, and a converted stem whose sum no longer matches its stored mix fails the integrity check. Evidence: the sum-to-mixture and integrity tests in the Linux PR run.
An ACE extract output carries origin regenerated_part and the label 'new performance', and never 'isolated'. Evidence: the labelling test in CI.
Isolation in an llc project is refused with its reason, and a RoFormer checkpoint not on the allow-list is refused before load. Evidence: the refusal tests in CI.
Preflight reserves the stem estimate before a separation starts, and refuses when it does not fit. Evidence: the preflight test in CI.
Stems insert onto tracks, a stem downloads, and stem-to-MIDI yields a MelodySpec-like clip with confidences. Evidence: the Playwright and harness tests in CI.

Bleed and residual-energy thresholds are read from the committed gate record (a test fails on a hard-coded threshold), and a stem's label is 'separated · unreviewed' without a listening record. Evidence: the threshold-source and label tests in CI.
tickets.notes: P5-4. ADR-0006, ADR-0029, GAP-06. Re-perform and Create a new part are v2 (ADR-0006); only their origins (reserved in the contracts) and the labelling guards are in v1. Split in the design review: the real isolation on Jon's keeper, with his listening verdict, is its own ticket.

tickets.title: Isolate original on Jon's keeper: a real separation, its thresholds, and Jon's listening verdict on stems, residual and rebuilt mix (needs Jon)
tickets.what_to_build: Stems are labelled isolated only after a real separation passed its thresholds and Jon listened. On Jon's keeper, a real isolate-original runs on the Mac; bleed and residual energy are measured against the committed thresholds; Jon listens to each stem, the residual and the rebuilt mix and records a verdict. The record lifts the 'separated · unreviewed' label for that separator revision. Why blocked: T52 (Jon's first real keeper, and through it the real separators on the Mac); T85 (isolate original and its checks).
acceptance_criteria: The isolation record holds bleed and residual-energy figures against the committed thresholds and the integrity sum on the stored files. Evidence: the evidence record id under docs/evidence/.
Jon's verdict on the stems, residual and rebuilt mix is recorded as an owner act, and the label changes only with it. Evidence: the verdict record id and a screenshot attached to the PR.
tickets.notes: Needs Jon: his keeper and his listening. Split from the isolate-original ticket in the design review. ADR-0006, O-06.
tickets.owner_needs: Chooses the keeper; listens to the stems, the residual and the rebuilt mix and gives a verdict.

tickets.title: Aligned stem and track export: a common rate, zero start and equal frame counts, checked automatically
tickets.what_to_build: A DAW can take the song over cleanly. The Export sheet gains aligned stems and tracks: every file at one common rate, starting at zero, with equal frame counts, the residual included, rendered by the offline render and listed in the ExportManifest with roles stem and residual. An automated check verifies the zero start and equal frame counts of every file before the bundle is offered. Each stem's release blockers reach the manifest (Demucs-isolated stems are release-blocked until Jon decides otherwise). Why blocked: T33 (the export sheet, Score.manifest and the export task it extends); T81 (tracks come from the offline render); T85 (stems and their residual to export).
acceptance_criteria: Every exported stem and track has the same rate and frame count and starts at frame zero, and a planted one-frame offset fails the check. Evidence: the alignment tests in the Linux PR run.
Stems plus residual in the bundle sum to the exported mix within the declared domain. Evidence: the sum test in CI.
The manifest lists each stem and the residual with role, rate, frames and hash. Evidence: the manifest test in CI.
tickets.notes: P5-5's DAW-import screenshots belong to Jon's first song (owner-gated), because they need his DAW.

tickets.title: DSP finishing: gain, fades, EQ, trimming and conversion as jobs, a numeric loudness meter, explicit loudness targets with the dry export kept, and finishing an imported mix
tickets.what_to_build: Jon finishes by measurement, and processing is always his choice and always reversible. S11 Finishing applies gain, fades, EQ, trimming and format or rate conversion as deterministic dsp-finish jobs that never change what was performed. A loudness and true-peak meter with numeric readouts sits in S10 and S11. At export Jon may choose a loudness target for a destination (for example -14 LUFS); the dry export is always included and no target is ever applied silently. No generative enhancement or super-resolution is applied by default. DSP finishing means what O-08 says: non-generative mixing and mastering, and format. An imported mix can be finished the same way, and a set of Jon's own Suno stems can be imported together and mixed: a Suno import only by DSP finishing, with its embedded provenance marks preserved and its imported terms carried into the manifest; a DAW bounce under the lanes of the exports it contains. Placing a Suno import on a timeline beside AURA-generated audio is refused unless a risk acceptance names edit input. Any generative operation on an imported mix is refused. Why blocked: T33 (loudness targets and the dry export are export options, and the loudness-target section fills an Export-sheet slot); T64 (imported mixes, their attested terms and allowed uses); T77 (the Studio's loudness meter sits in the timeline).
acceptance_criteria: A dsp-finish chain on a generated signal equals a hand-computed result (bit-exact within one environment). Evidence: the DSP tests in the Linux PR run.
An export with a -14 LUFS target contains both the targeted file and the untouched dry file, and the loudness report names the standard and meter. Evidence: the export test in CI.
A DSP-finished stand-in Suno import keeps its embedded metadata byte-identical and its export manifest carries Suno's terms; a cover request on it is refused. Evidence: the import tests in CI.
The meters expose numeric values, and S11 passes the accessibility audit and the keyboard-only pass. Evidence: the Playwright accessibility report in CI.

A stand-in Suno stem set imports as one set with the Suno limits, mixes non-generatively, and a timeline combining it with an AURA candidate is refused without a risk acceptance. Evidence: the stem-set and combination tests in CI.
tickets.notes: P5-6. ADR-0019, ADR-0021, ADR-0036. Tests use synthetic stand-ins; Jon's real Suno download is finished in his first-song ticket. No Matchering in v1. ADR-0019, ADR-0020 (Suno output is never training data).

tickets.title: Operator lanes end to end: the lane change as an owner act, branching a song from a keeper, and one negative test per enforcement point
tickets.what_to_build: A lane leak would take seven bugs, not one. `POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/lane` is an owner act (O6 Lane change dialog) that re-checks every artifact and every lane-carrying record in the project (a MelodySpec drafted by a lane-restricted transcriber carries that transcriber's lanes through every revision built on it) and is refused with the list of artifacts and records that block it. Jon can start a new project from a keeper revision, carrying its closure, checked against the new project's lane.
